epic.title: Bring the Office to Life
epic.objective:
Transform Coffee Break's functional virtual office into an expressive, readable workspace where agents communicate their state and activity primarily through character behavior, workstation feedback, contextual visual language, and environmental interactions.

EP-03 made trusted agent state technically correct.

EP-04 makes that trusted state feel alive while preserving semantic truth.

historical_story.title: Establish the Living Office Design Direction

stories.title: Express Agent State Through Visual Vocabulary
stories.user_story: As a Coffee Break user, I want agents to visibly express their current lifecycle state, so that I can understand what is happening in the office at a glance without depending on developer-like status UI.
stories.objective:
Implement the approved behavior-led character vocabulary for:

- idle
- working
- waiting
- completed
- error

Character behavior is the primary broad-state signal.

Precise trusted information remains available through inspection.
acceptance_criteria:
Five lifecycle states

All five trusted lifecycle states have intentional character-level presentation and are meaningfully distinguishable without depending on persistent lifecycle text below each agent.

Idle semantics

Idle presents a calm/ready agent and must not imply sleeping, coffee, assigned work, completion, or disconnection.

Working semantics

Working uses restrained operational character behavior without implying measured progress, coding specifically, successful output, or a particular provider operation.

Waiting semantics

Waiting stops working behavior and presents an attentive/paused state.

Generic waiting must not imply coffee, approval, capacity exhaustion, failure, or completion.

Completed semantics

Entering completed may trigger one brief acknowledgement and then settles into stable completed presentation.

The transient acknowledgement must not replay merely because of rerender, selection, retained-state restoration, synchronization restoration, or presentation remount without a new meaningful lifecycle transition.

Error semantics

Entering error may trigger one brief attention reaction and then settles.

It must not fabricate hardware failure, data loss, a crash, root cause, or provider-specific meaning.

Supporting cues

Symbols/comic accents are secondary reinforcement.

Meaning must not depend solely on color, animation, hover, or glyph familiarity.

Live versus retained presentation

Operational repeating character animation runs only while presentation is live.

Retained last-known lifecycle remains visible while operational loops pause.

Connection state must not mutate lifecycle.

Reduced motion

Reduced motion removes unnecessary repeating/transient motion while preserving meaningful static state treatment and precise textual information.

Runtime authority

Trusted renderer agent state remains runtime authority.

Do not introduce a parallel lifecycle state source inside Phaser.

Selection independence

Selection, keyboard focus, lifecycle, and availability remain separate.

Changing selection must not mutate or restart lifecycle behavior.

Verification

Automated coverage verifies deterministic derivation/transition behavior where practical.

Developer demonstrates all five states, retained presentation, and reduced motion.

Designer review verifies visual meaning against US-019.
stories.boundary: No real providers, new lifecycle states, personalities, voice/chat, autonomous movement/pathfinding, generalized workstation redesign, general contextual interaction system, fake operational data, GitHub features, themes/rooms, or application-shell redesign.
definition_of_done: focused automated tests added/updated where appropriate;
independent Reviewer review completed after design findings are resolved;

stories.title: Make Agent Workstations Reactive
stories.user_story: As a Coffee Break user, I want an agent's immediate workspace to react consistently with the agent's state, so that the office feels inhabited without displaying fabricated operational information.
stories.objective:
Implement restrained workstation/environment reinforcement for trusted broad lifecycle state.

Character behavior from US-020 remains the primary signal.
acceptance_criteria:
Idle workstation

Idle has a stable quiet workstation treatment without implying active work, sleep, failure, or completion.

Working workstation

Working may use restrained abstract monitor activity.

It must not resemble or claim readable code, terminal output, logs, messages, progress percentages, token/model information, or productivity metrics.

Waiting workstation

Waiting stops active working workstation behavior and may retain a stable paused treatment.

Completed workstation

Completed may briefly acknowledge the state and settle into a stable completed treatment without claiming measured output or productivity.

Error workstation

Error may use restrained attention treatment without inventing hardware failure, crash, data loss, or root cause.

Atomic consistency

Character and workstation presentation derive from the same trusted broad lifecycle situation.

Contradictory combinations such as waiting character + actively working monitor are not permitted.

Retained state

Repeating workstation activity pauses for retained/non-live presentation while stable last-known treatment remains.

Returning live must not fabricate lifecycle transitions.

Environmental restraint

Prioritize existing desks, monitors, and immediate work context.

General room decoration remains mostly static.

Sol semantics

Do not invent a third workstation for Sol.

Sol's coffee context belongs to US-022.

Reduced motion

Provide meaningful static workstation treatment when reduced motion is active.

Verification

Test lifecycle-to-workstation derivation and contradictory-state prevention where practical.

Designer verifies that workstation effects reinforce rather than compete with character behavior.
stories.boundary: No fake code/logs, operational metrics, progress indicators, model/token data, generalized environmental simulation, third Sol workstation, new trusted event fields, provider integration, or autonomous movement.
definition_of_done: focused automated tests added/updated where appropriate;
independent Reviewer review completed after design findings are resolved;

stories.title: Add Contextual Office Interactions
stories.user_story: As a Coffee Break user, I want explicit agent context to produce small meaningful interactions with the office, so that trusted activity feels connected to the environment.
stories.objective: Introduce the smallest maintainable contextual-presentation mechanism and implement the first canonical contextual interaction: Sol's explicit coffee fixture.
dependency_notes: US-021 where existing environment primitives are reused
acceptance_criteria:
Explicit context

A context-specific office interaction requires explicit trusted presentation context.

Lifecycle alone cannot authorize it.

Sol coffee fixture

Coffee presentation is authorized only for the existing conjunction:

agent: mock-agent-sol

lifecycle: waiting

activity: Taking a coffee break in the simulated office

Generic waiting

Generic waiting uses neutral waiting presentation and does not produce coffee-specific behavior.

Generic idle

Idle does not imply coffee or break behavior.

Trusted inspection

During coffee presentation, trusted lifecycle remains waiting and exact activity remains unchanged in inspection.

Do not introduce a break lifecycle state.

Coffee expression

The presentation may use mug/cup, coffee-area context, restrained steam, and optional sparse polish such as a brief "sip" accent.

Such polish must not be required for comprehension or permanently shown.

Bounded mechanism

Implement only the smallest maintainable presentation-level mechanism needed to map explicit trusted context to a micro-interaction.

Do not create a generalized behavior engine or scheduler.

No autonomous movement

No pathfinding, general walking, autonomous wandering, meetings, room navigation, or command scheduling.

Use approved existing presentation anchors.

Freshness and reduced motion

Repeating contextual motion pauses when retained/non-live.

Reduced motion provides a stable equivalent.

Selection semantics

Selection feedback must not imply the agent received an instruction.

Verification

Tests cover the exact Sol fixture and negative cases for generic waiting, idle, and other agents.

Designer verifies the interaction feels environmental/contextual rather than dashboard-like.
stories.boundary: No new provider events, break lifecycle, navigation/pathfinding, personalities, voice/chat, task assignment, meetings, or generalized interaction scheduler.
definition_of_done: focused automated tests added/updated where appropriate;
independent Reviewer review completed after design findings are resolved;

stories.title: Integrate Agent Information Into the Office Experience
stories.user_story: As a Coffee Break user, I want selection and detailed agent information to feel integrated with the virtual office, so that I can inspect precise trusted information without the application feeling like a monitoring dashboard.
stories.objective: Implement approved Treatment C identity hierarchy, selection treatment, compact selector, contextual inspector, availability presentation, and responsive composition.
acceptance_criteria:
Persistent identity

Ari, Mina, and Sol retain compact persistent identity associated with their characters.

Do not restore permanent full lifecycle/activity paragraphs beneath every agent.

In-world selection

Direct sprite selection remains supported.

Selection is visually distinct from lifecycle, availability, and keyboard focus and does not depend solely on color.

Compact selector

Provide compact named accessible controls for Ari, Mina, and Sol with accessible names, selected/pressed state, and visible keyboard focus.

Do not use large portrait roster cards as the default treatment.

Selection consistency

Sprite and selector selection address the same identity and inspection state.

Lifecycle updates do not unexpectedly clear selection.

Selection does not unexpectedly move keyboard focus.

No trusted state

Without trusted agent state, use explicit unavailable treatment.

Do not fabricate lifecycle or activity.

Retained information

Preserve and explicitly qualify last-known information.

Disconnection must not map lifecycle to idle, waiting, or error.

Operational loops follow the freshness behavior established by prior stories.

Long content

Long activity, reason, and availability text wraps without overlap or horizontal overflow.

Accessibility

Important information remains available without hover, color, or animation.

Preserve named keyboard controls, visible focus, textual lifecycle equivalents, precise trusted inspection, and appropriate polite announcements.

Do not claim screen-reader correctness without actual verification.

Reduced motion

Composition remains usable with reduced motion and preserves clear live-versus-last-known meaning.

Verification

Validate actual application behavior at both 1100 × 760 and 760 × 540.

Designer reviews both sizes.
stories.boundary: No dashboard metrics, model/token/cost/productivity data, GitHub/project board, provider controls, chat/voice, label-preference setting, unapproved keyboard shortcuts, or architecture redesign.
definition_of_done: focused automated tests added/updated where appropriate;
independent Reviewer review completed after design findings are resolved;

stories.title: Verify and Polish the Living Office Experience
stories.user_story: As a Coffee Break user, I want the complete Living Office experience to remain coherent across agent state, selection, availability, window size, and accessibility modes, so that the office feels reliable and finished.
stories.objective:
Perform integrated EP-04 verification and bounded polish for US-020 through US-023.

This is not a feature-expansion story.
acceptance_criteria:
Integrated lifecycle journey

Verify idle, working, waiting, completed, and error presentation.

Broad state remains understandable in the office while precise trusted information remains available through inspection.

Workstation consistency

Verify workstation/environment cues remain synchronized with character presentation through transitions.

Contextual coffee behavior

Verify the canonical Sol fixture produces coffee presentation and negative cases do not.

Selection journey

Verify sprite selection, selector selection, clear selection, lifecycle updates while selected, and availability changes while selected.

Connection/retained journey

Verify connecting, synchronized, interruption, retained synchronization, disconnected-retained, unavailable, and return-to-live behavior.

Retained state remains visible and qualified while operational loops pause.

No connection transition fabricates lifecycle.

One-shot effects

Verify completed/error acknowledgements do not replay due solely to selection, rerender, remount/restoration, or resynchronization without a new meaningful lifecycle transition.

Normal window

Verify actual behavior at 1100 × 760 including office dominance, side inspection, selector weight, availability hierarchy, long content, pixel rendering, and focus.

Minimum window

Verify actual behavior at 760 × 540 including no horizontal overflow, readable office, immediate selected identity/lifecycle feedback, vertical access to full inspector, reachable controls, wrapping, and no clipped essential content.

Reduced motion

Verify representative lifecycle, workstation, contextual, and retained situations under reduced motion.

Keyboard/focus

Verify selector reachability, visible focus, selection/focus distinction, clear-selection behavior, and that updates do not unexpectedly move focus or pan the document.

Accessibility evidence

Verify textual equivalents and appropriate live/status announcements in the actual application.

Record exact environment and observed behavior for any screen-reader test.

Do not claim unperformed assistive-technology verification.

Design review

Designer reviews integrated implementation against the North Star and approved US-019 design documentation.

Regression

Existing EP-03 trusted-event, synchronization, deduplication, security, connection, and simulator behavior remains intact.

Run repository typecheck, lint, tests, build, and appropriate integration checks.

Verification record

Record EP-04 verification evidence and distinguish automated evidence, Developer observations, Designer review, Product Owner/user-assisted observations, and unverified behavior.

Scope discipline

Polish may fix implementation defects and small approved-design inconsistencies only.

Material new product/design/architecture requirements return to the appropriate planning workflow.
stories.boundary: No real providers, new lifecycle semantics, personalities, voice/chat, task assignment, general movement/pathfinding, rooms/themes, GitHub integration, operational statistics, or major architecture redesign.
definition_of_done: US-024 uses its own integrated verification criteria as the final EP-04 acceptance story.
